title: SYSK Distraction Playlist: Sugar: It Powers the Earth
summary: A Stuff You Should Know distraction playlist episode, presented as a compilation of favorite past episodes not yet released as select. The hosts cover sugar: its origins in New Guinea and Polynesia, spread through India, the Crusades, and Columbus to the Caribbean, its ties to slavery, its early luxury status and Venetian trade, the effects of the Reformation and tea culture in Britain, and sugar beets versus sugarcane processing (crystallization, centrifuges, molasses, bagasse, sugar dust explosions). They also discuss types of sugar (sucrose, glucose, fructose, lactose, sugar alcohols, icing and preserving sugar), high fructose corn syrup and metabolic syndrome, sugar and tooth decay, sugar-based ethanol in Brazil, and microbial fuel cells. The episode closes with a listener mail rebuttal on creationism and evolution (micro versus macro evolution).

segments.title: Playlist opening and sugar banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the distraction playlist of past favorite episodes and open with banter about sweet nicknames, The Simpsons, and tasting sugar.

segments.title: Origins and spread of sugar
segments.summary: Sugar is traced to New Guinea and Polynesia, then spread through Indonesia and India, via Persian conquest, the Crusades, and Columbus bringing sugarcane to the Caribbean. The hosts note its links to the slave trade.

segments.title: Sugar as luxury and rise in Britain
segments.summary: Sugar was once a royal luxury. Venice sold fifty tons to England in 1319. The Reformation closed monasteries and sugar became widely available, which boosted tea drinking in Britain.

segments.title: Sugar beets and sugarcane processing
segments.summary: The hosts compare sugar beets (about 17 percent sugar) and sugarcane (about 10 percent). They describe extraction, boiling, filtering, centrifuging crystals from mother liquor, and the sugar dust explosion at a Savannah refinery.

segments.title: Molasses, bagasse, and byproducts
segments.summary: Molasses is a byproduct that gives brown sugar its color and is used to make rum. Bagasse, the leftover cane pulp, is burned as fuel to power refineries, though the industry's deforestation and labor impacts are noted.

segments.title: Types of sugar and sugar alcohols
segments.summary: The hosts list sucrose, glucose, fructose, and lactose, and where each is found. They discuss sugar alcohols such as xylitol, the sugar-free gum brand, and granulations including icing, castor, granulated, and preserving sugar. A digression on Bluebell ice cream follows.

segments.title: High fructose corn syrup, metabolism, and health
segments.summary: The hosts explain why high fructose corn syrup may be worse than sugar: the liver converts fructose to fat, and the syrup form hits the liver fast. They discuss metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and the claim that sugar is a heart disease risk.

segments.title: Sugar, taste, and tooth decay
segments.summary: The hosts describe how sugar binds to sweet taste receptors, how plants use sugar, and how bacteria, including Streptococcus mutans, feed on sugar and produce lactic acid that erodes enamel and causes cavities.

segments.title: Sugar as fuel and microbial fuel cells
segments.summary: Brazil ran on sugarcane ethanol, and the hosts discuss the competition between fuel and food prices. Microbes that eat sugar can release electrons to produce current, which the hosts describe as a possible future power source.
